title: Stream consistency primitive and client mental models (PRD draft)
content:
Context and problem statement:

We continue to get signals from SDK and integrations teams that developers struggle to form a reliable mental model around partial/streaming responses when tool calls and structured outputs are involved. Common symptoms: clients drop partial state, duplicate tool calls on reconnect, and parsers mis-handle provisional JSON fragments. This leads to broken user flows (e.g., duplicate DB writes via a tool call), fragile client code, and higher support overhead.

Goal (product outcome):
- Define and ship a minimal "stream consistency primitive" in the Hosted API that codifies partial output semantics, tool-call idempotency hooks, and a small set of ergonomic SDK surfaces for safe resumption and graceful backoff.
- Reduce integration support tickets related to streaming replays and tool duplication by 50% in the first quarter after rollout.
- Provide a migration path that doesn't require rewriting existing SDK callers.

Non-goals:
- Not a full transactional protocol. We will not guarantee cross-request distributed transactions.
- Not a heavy-weight message broker; this is still an HTTP/streaming surface.

Principles guiding the design:
- Minimal primitives: expose a few simple signals clients can reason about.
- Fail-safe by default: server behavior should prefer idempotency and explicitness to avoid silent duplicates.
- SDK-first ergonomics: provide conventions that reduce boilerplate and accidental misuse.
- Backwards compatible: current non-streaming and naive streaming clients keep working.

Key concepts and API signals (proposal):
1) Frame types: every streaming response is a sequence of typed frames. Frames are small, monotonic, and strictly ordered. Frame types include:
   - META: connection/session metadata emitted first (session id, model, schema version).
   - DELTA: incremental textual tokens or partial structured payloads. DELTA frames may carry a "fragment" flag when content is incomplete at schema token boundaries.
   - CHECKPOINT: explicit, application-level stable points that indicate the server considers the partial output "materialized" for downstream actions (tool-calls, DB writes). CHECKPOINT includes a monotonic checkpoint_id.
   - CALL: a tool-call intent frame; contains tool_id, args (structured), and an idempotency_key. CALL frames MUST be followed by CHECKPOINT to indicate they were durably scheduled/executed.
   - RESUME_HINT: optional, server-provided hint for client reconnection strategy (e.g., resume_from=checkpoint_id, or full-restart).
   - ERROR/CLOSE: terminal frames.

2) Checkpoint semantics:
   - CHECKPOINT frames are the authoritative signal for side-effecting work: until CHECKPOINT is observed, clients should not assume tool actions have occurred.
   - CHECKPOINT ids are monotonic per-session and stable across short reconnections (see session id below).

3) Session model and short-lived session ids:
   - Each streaming call emits a session_id in META. A session_id is valid for N seconds/minutes (configurable) and allows resume attempts to reference recent checkpoints.
   - Resume is best-effort: if the server retained the session state, RESUME_HINT with resume_from checkpoint_id will be provided. If not, server will recommend restart.

4) Tool-call idempotency and safe replays:
   - Each CALL frame MUST include an idempotency_key (UUID or client-provided stable key). Service guarantees: if server receives the same idempotency_key within the same session and the CALL has reached CHECKPOINT, it will not re-execute the tool.
   - If client reconnects and resends the same CALL prior to seeing CHECKPOINT, server can deduplicate if it has the request and can respond with a past CALL result plus CHECKPOINT replay.
   - For cross-session idempotency, Clients should include a stable idempotency prefix to enable dedup across short-lived session rotation. We will document tradeoffs.

5) Structured incremental JSON strategy:
   - DELTA frames carrying structured output will follow a "fragmented-json" convention: server emits JSON text fragments with explicit fragment markers when tokens do not align to a top-level object boundary. The SDK will provide a small parser that buffers until a full object is observed or a CHECKPOINT commits partial structured objects as "provisional".
   - Schema version included in META to help client parsers decide strict vs lenient merge.

SDK surface proposals (client ergonomics):
- High-level SDK streaming client provides:
  1) on_partial(delta): called for each DELTA; SDK handles streaming text concat and fragmented-json buffering.
  2) on_checkpoint(checkpoint_id, summary): called when a CHECKPOINT arrives. Default behavior: update local transcript and expose stable output.
  3) on_tool_call(tool_payload, idempotency_key): SDK will expose helper to transform CALL frames into a safe invocation that tracks idempotency and returns a future/promise that completes only when CHECKPOINT is observed.
  4) resume(session_id, resume_from_checkpoint_id): convenience that handles reconnection backoff, poll for resume hint, and rehydrates any pending CALL promises.

Developer ergonomics patterns (examples):
- Simple viewer: wants to show partial text only; uses on_partial and ignores CALL. Works without changes.
- Side-effecting workflow: a server may propose a CALL to a database writer. Using SDK helper, the app calls the tool adapter which returns a promise; app awaits the promise only after on_checkpoint ensures the tool was durable. If the client disconnects and resumes, SDK ensures the promise resolves once CHECKPOINT is observed (or errors on timeout).

Failure modes and how we handle them:
- Client reconnects and server has no session state: RESUME_HINT will suggest full restart. SDK should surface a clear error to the app and optionally replay prompts.
- CHECKPOINT lost in transit: use monotonic checkpoint ids and idempotency_key: resending CALL with same idempotency_key within window avoids duplicates (server dedup behavior). Telemetry will log mismatches.
- Partial JSON parse errors: SDK parser will expose both raw fragments and a best-effort merged object; default is to surface a parse error and provisional payload for debugging.

Observability and telemetry requirements:
- Emit events: session.start, frame.delivered(type), checkpoint.observed(session_id, checkpoint_id), call.scheduled(idempotency_key), call.executed(idempotency_key), resume.attempt, resume.success/fail.
- Tag traces with session_id and checkpoint_id for end-to-end debugging.
- Add a small dashboard tile in Console listing streaming stability: avg resume success rate, duplicate-call incidents, avg time-to-checkpoint.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Spec-complete and SDK beta (0–4 weeks): finalize frame spec and implement reference parser/client in JS and Python.
2) Invite early adopters + partner integrations (4–8 weeks): offer opt-in streaming flag; gather feedback and fix edge cases.
3) Progressive opt-in for new streaming endpoints (8–12 weeks): enable default for new endpoints; keep old streaming path intact.
4) Opt-out deprecation (12–20 weeks): after stability signals, make primitive the recommended/standard streaming contract; document migration steps.

Open questions and tradeoffs for review:
- Checkpoint frequency: fine-grained checkpoints reduce replay window but increase control plane noise. Proposal: configurable checkpoint hints in model routing layer; default every X tokens or at tool-call boundaries.
- State retention window for resume: how long should the control plane keep session state? Costs vs reliability tradeoff. Propose 10 minutes default with enterprise SLA option.
- Cross-region resume semantics: how do we surface resume when traffic shifts across regions? Likely fall back to restart; explore sticky routing for sessions.

Next steps / action items:
- (Alyssa) draft RPC/frame protobuf + text spec for review (this doc).
- (Jonah) prototype JS SDK streaming parser + checkpoint helpers (due in 2 weeks).
- (Priya) design telemetry events and Console tile mock (due in 2 weeks).
- (Marco) cost model for retention window + checkpoint frequency (due in 1 week).

Appendix: rough example stream transcript (illustrative)
META {"session_id": "s_1234", "schema_v": "v2"}
DELTA {"text": "Analyzing input..."}
DELTA {"text": "Found two candidates:"}
CALL {"tool": "web-search", "args": {"q": "latest release notes"}, "idempotency_key": "c-789"}
CHECKPOINT {"checkpoint_id": 5, "summary": "search scheduled"}
DELTA {"text": "Synthesizing answer..."}
CALL {"tool": "db-write", "args": {"record": {"id": 42}}, "idempotency_key": "c-790"}
CHECKPOINT {"checkpoint_id": 6, "summary": "writes applied"}
DELTA {"text": "Response ready."}
CLOSE {"code": 0}

This PRD is intentionally focused on a small set of primitives to reduce developer cognitive load while enabling safe tool workflows and structured incremental output. Feedback requested: checkpoint cadence, default client behaviors on resume, and required SLA for session retention.

-- end of draft --
